policy_title: Maintain High Food Standards in Trade Deals
stated: Maintain high health, environmental and animal welfare standards in food production and guarantee that all future trade deals will meet them too, ensuring that Britain’s farmers and food manufacturers are not put at an unfair disadvantage.

source.quote: Maintain high health, environmental and animal welfare standards in food production and guarantee that all future trade deals will meet them too, ensuring that Britain’s farmers and food manufacturers are not put at an unfair disadvantage.

bearing_set.reason: The policy explicitly targets environmental and animal welfare standards in food production and trade deals, directly affecting whether lower-standard (higher-impact) food can enter the UK market.

The stated objective of protecting British farmers and food manufacturers from unfair competition by lower-standard imports directly affects agricultural livelihoods, employment, and fair competitive conditions.

Blocking lower-standard (potentially cheaper) imports — e.g. hormone-treated beef, chlorinated chicken — sustains higher domestic food prices for consumers, a real and contested cost-of-living trade-off.

Conditioning all future trade deals on high standards narrows the universe of viable trading partners (e.g. US, Brazil may not accept such conditions), reducing the economic gains from trade liberalisation — a concrete constraint on economic opportunity and real living standards over the medium to long term.

membership_note: Four fundamentals bear genuinely: the policy's protective intent (O4, O6) is clear from its text, while the tradeoffs on consumer food prices (O2) and aggregate trade-driven prosperity (O13) are mechanistically grounded and non-negligible.
